narrative: OMX30 faces a classic bull-bear tug-of-war. Technicals remain constructive—BULL MARKET regime, +5.9% above 200-MA, MACD bullish, ROC-90 at +7.5%—but macro headwinds are intensifying. Global equity weakness (weighted correlation -0.365%) and surging US yields (+3bp) create DCF drag on tech and real estate. The USD/SEK strength (+0.74%) is a tailwind for industrials and pharma exporters, but oil's jump to $105 (+1.82%) pressures input costs and consumer demand. VIX's +7.18% jump to 16.27 signals rising risk-aversion despite OMX30's technical resilience. Watch for mean reversion risk if yields continue climbing; ADX weakness (0.0) means conviction is thin. Trade tariff escalation remains the tail risk that could snap the 5.9% rally.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to a mixed macro backdrop: technicals support a small rally (+0.2%), but elevated US yields and global equity weakness cap upside. Key levels: 3180 (50-MA resistance), 3123 (pivot), 3085 (lower Bollinger). Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Sandvik) benefit from USD/SEK strength but face headwinds from oil-driven input costs. Banks rally on wider NIM outlook (SEB A, Handelsbanken A positive), but real estate (Balder, Castellum) weakens on refinancing anxiety. Tech/Telecom (Ericsson, Hexagon) risk rotation out given NASDAQ weakness and DCF compression. Boliden is your commodity play—copper +1.01%, gold firm. Watch US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET for directional cues; any disappointment could trigger VIX spike and unwind the rally. Keep risk tight; ADX signals weak conviction.
